# Côte d’Ivoire Cocoa Case Validation

## Short answer

**Recommendation: validate further.** The **EUDR/traceability layer is strong enough for an internal benchmark slide**, because there is primary-source evidence of an official producer-card and unified traceability rollout, a national sustainable cocoa policy/strategy stack, an EU Sustainable Cocoa Initiative with Côte d’Ivoire, and a clear EUDR compliance frame around geolocation and deforestation-free due diligence. However, the **direct Natural State / Nordic Circular Hotspot / WCEF relationship layer is not yet fact-voice ready**: in the material reviewed, I did **not** find a public signed MOU, agreement PDF, programme page, meeting note, or partner-side confirmation that formally links Natural State, Nordic Circular Hotspot, NCH or WCEF to a Côte d’Ivoire cocoa programme. The only direct relation signal found is a **Natural State organisation LinkedIn post** saying it was in Côte d’Ivoire to sign an MOU with **LEAD Ivory Coast** during a visit that included cocoa-related field exposure; without the actual MOU or counterparty confirmation, that remains a **relation hypothesis** rather than documented case evidence. On **rest streams**, there is real signal, but it is still **pilot / project-pipeline / company-specific**, not a proven scaled national solution. citeturn56view0turn52view4turn48view1turn56view1turn25search1turn29view2turn23search0turn24search0turn36search2turn33search0turn26view1turn55view0turn19search4

**Working decision by claim cluster**

- **Relation claim:** keep as **needs-actor-validation / needs-primary-check**.
- **EUDR / traceability claim:** **deckklart internt** as a benchmark case.
- **Nordic company-role claim:** partially documented, but mixed depth; use selectively and mark company-specific gaps.
- **Rest-stream claim:** **watchlist** or **benchmark-only** unless pilot owners confirm implementation stage, volumes, and actors. citeturn36search2turn56view1turn56view0turn25search1turn55view1turn26view4turn17search14turn26view1turn19search4

| **EUDR — Cocoa, cocoa waste and derivatives are in scope, and geolocation of plots is required** | **Documented fact.** The EUDR annex covers cocoa beans, cocoa shells/husks/skins and other cocoa waste, cocoa paste, butter, powder and chocolate; Article 9 requires geolocation of all plots of land where the relevant commodities were produced. citeturn28view0turn29view2 | Official Journal / EUR-Lex Regulation (EU) 2023/1115. citeturn28view0turn29view2 | Cocoa and cocoa waste streams are legally in scope; due diligence requires plot-level location data. citeturn28view0turn29view2 | It does **not** prove that Côte d’Ivoire actors are currently compliant. | **documented fact; deckklart internt** |
| **EUDR — Current application timing still makes Côte d’Ivoire cocoa compliance strategically relevant** | **Documented fact.** The Commission’s current EUDR page says application starts on **30 December 2026** for large/medium operators and **30 June 2027** for micro/small operators; the 2025 amending regulation updates Article 38 accordingly. citeturn25search1turn27view0 | European Commission EUDR page; amending Regulation (EU) 2025/2650. citeturn25search1turn27view0 | The compliance clock has shifted, but the requirement remains live and time-bound. citeturn25search1turn27view0 | It does **not** prove country readiness. | **documented fact; deckklart internt** |
| **Deforestation — Cocoa is a major documented deforestation risk in Côte d’Ivoire** | **Documented fact.** The Nature Food study links cocoa to over **37%** of forest loss in protected areas in Côte d’Ivoire from 2000–2020. A World Bank-supported PIF2 strategy document for Côte d’Ivoire states cocoa is responsible for **60%** of national deforestation and that **40%** of cocoa comes from classified forests and protected areas. citeturn23search0turn52view1 | Nature Food paper; official PIF2 strategy document hosted by Ministry of Waters and Forests. citeturn23search0turn52view1 | Cocoa-linked deforestation risk is not speculative; it is central to the case. citeturn23search0turn52view1 | The figures come from different methods and are not interchangeable. | **documented fact; deckklart internt** |
| **Value-chain relevance — Côte d’Ivoire cocoa is materially tied to the EU market** | **Documented fact.** The EU programming annex states that **67% of Ivorian cocoa exports go to the EU**, and the EU partnership page says the sustainable cocoa initiative aims to help the value chain comply with EU regulation. citeturn56view1turn48view2 | EU programming annex; EU Côte d’Ivoire partnership page. citeturn56view1turn48view2 | EU market relevance is major and directly linked to sustainability and compliance. citeturn56view1turn48view2 | It does **not** quantify the Nordic share inside EU demand. | **documented fact; deckklart internt** |

## Guardrails, next actions and search strings

**“Do not say” list**

- “Natural State / Nordic Circular Hotspot has a documented signed Côte d’Ivoire cocoa MOU.” The reviewed public evidence stops at a Natural State organisation post saying an MOU was being signed with LEAD Ivory Coast; the actual signed document was not found. citeturn36search2turn33search0
- “WCEF has an official Côte d’Ivoire cocoa programme with Natural State / NCH.” I did not find a primary-source WCEF programme page supporting that. The official NCH project pages reviewed do not establish it. citeturn33search0turn33search18
- “Nordic governments are materially leading sustainable cocoa programming in Côte d’Ivoire.” In the official material reviewed, only **Finland** is clearly documented inside the Team Europe cocoa architecture. citeturn48view2turn56view1
- “Nordic import dependence from Côte d’Ivoire is quantified here.” EU-level dependence is documented; Nordic bilateral import tables were **not** established in this pass. citeturn56view1turn48view2
- “Côte d’Ivoire’s traceability problem is solved.” The policy stack and rollout are real, but public analytics still show major disclosure / traceability gaps. citeturn56view0turn24search0turn24search1
- “Cocoa residue valorisation is already a scaled national circular solution in Côte d’Ivoire.” The evidence found points to project pipeline, pilots and processor-specific uses, not national scale. citeturn26view1turn55view0turn19search3turn19search4
- “Orkla, Cloetta or Fazer have publicly disclosed Côte d’Ivoire sourcing volumes here.” The reviewed public material shows programmes / risk framing, but not country-level volume disclosure. citeturn55view1turn26view4turn17search14

**Next five actions ranked by highest validation yield**

1. **Ask Natural State for the MOU file and counterpart metadata.** Request the signed PDF, date, signatories, scope note, and whether cocoa / circular bioeconomy is in scope. This is the single fastest way to validate or kill the relation claim. citeturn36search2
2. **Ask LEAD Ivory Coast for counterparty confirmation.** Request the same MOU, plus any partner-side post, concept note, or implementation record. This will immediately separate “travel relation” from “case foundation.” citeturn36search2
3. **Request the current CCC traceability package.** Specifically: producer-card rollout totals, geolocation coverage, exporter/co-op interoperability, ARS1000 certification uptake, and any EUDR readiness note shared with exporters. citeturn56view0turn54search6turn32search21
4. **Run targeted company validation with Fazer, Cloetta and Orkla.** Ask for current Côte d’Ivoire supplier geography, co-op names, certification route, and whether they can share current traceability depth to plot or co-op level. citeturn55view1turn26view4turn17search14
5. **Contact CEA-VALOPRO / INP-HB and ofi on residue pilots.** Ask whether the biochar project has financing closed, pilot units installed, regions active, and what residue volumes are actually handled; separately ask ofi for the Côte d’Ivoire site and operating scale of shell-to-energy / biochar. citeturn26view1turn55view0turn19search4
